title: White House Confirms Trump Will Meet Modi on Wednesday at the G7. Trade, Visas and the Iran War Are All on the Table.
excerpt: It will be their first face-to-face meeting in over a year. The USTR will fly to India the following week to close a deal.
body:
The White House has confirmed that President Donald Trump will hold a bilateral meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday at the G7 summit in Évian-les-Bains, France. It will be the first face-to-face meeting between the two leaders since Modi's visit to Washington in February 2025 — and the first since India's military operation against Pakistan last year reshaped the regional security landscape.

A senior administration official, speaking during a briefing call with reporters on Saturday, laid out Trump's full G7 schedule: a bilateral with French President Emmanuel Macron on Monday, meetings with the Emir of Qatar, the Egyptian president and the UAE's emir on Tuesday, and then separate sit-downs with Egypt's el-Sisi and Modi on Wednesday. Notably absent from the schedule is a one-on-one meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, though the G7 leaders will meet with Zelensky as a group on Tuesday.

Trade Is the Headline, but Not the Only Line

!White House — Photo: Wikimedia Commons

The bilateral comes at a moment of genuine friction — and genuine opportunity — in the India-US relationship. Washington has proposed an additional 12.5 per cent tariff on Indian imports, alleging the use of forced labour, which India has categorically rejected. India, in turn, is pushing for preferential tariff treatment as part of an interim trade deal.

"Trump himself posted on Truth Social that "the Deal is scheduled to get signed tomorrow" and that the Hormuz Strait would reopen immediately after."

Yet momentum is building. U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer will travel to India the week after the G7, a senior U.S. official confirmed on Saturday, adding that a trade agreement was "possible." India's Trade Minister Piyush Goyal said last week that talks were moving towards the first tranche of a bilateral trade deal that could be concluded by mid-July.

The meeting will also come against the backdrop of India's sharp diplomatic confrontation with Washington over U.S. Navy strikes on merchant vessels in the Gulf that killed three Indian seafarers. External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar spoke to Secretary of State Marco Rubio this week, lodging a strong protest and calling the attacks "unjustified."

!The White House — Photo: Wikimedia Commons

The Iran Shadow

The entire G7 is being held under the shadow of the U.S.-Iran war. Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said on Saturday that a peace deal could be signed within 24 hours, though Iran's foreign ministry counselled caution on the timing. Trump himself posted on Truth Social that "the Deal is scheduled to get signed tomorrow" and that the Hormuz Strait would reopen immediately after.

For India, any resolution of the Iran crisis is existential. The conflict has spiked crude oil prices, blown a hole in India's fiscal deficit and killed Indian sailors on commercial vessels. Modi is expected to press Trump on maritime safety guarantees, energy pricing and the broader fallout for India's economy.

!President Donald Trump — Photo: Wikimedia Commons

The H-1B Question

The G7 sidelines are also expected to see a discussion on H-1B visas — a perennial concern for the Indian diaspora. A Republican lawmaker has introduced a bill to codify the $100,000 H-1B fee that a federal judge recently struck down. With immigration reform stalled in Congress and the Trump administration tightening enforcement, the Modi-Trump meeting may be one of the few channels left for India to make its case at the highest level.

What NRIs Should Watch For

This is a meeting that touches almost every dimension of diaspora life. Trade affects the companies Indian Americans work for. H-1B policy affects their colleagues, families and futures. The Iran conflict affects remittance corridors, oil prices and the safety of Indian workers in the Gulf. Whether Modi and Trump emerge with a handshake, a framework or just warm optics, the bilateral on Wednesday will set the tone for the next phase of the world's most consequential emerging relationship.
